title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Overview
text: Retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG, combines information retrieval with language generation. A retriever finds relevant context from a document collection, and a generator uses that context to produce an answer. RAG can reduce hallucination by grounding answers in retrieved passages and by exposing citations for inspection.

title: Document Chunking
text: Chunking splits long documents into smaller passages before indexing. Good chunks preserve local context while staying short enough for retrieval and generation. Overlapping windows can improve recall because important facts near chunk boundaries appear in more than one indexed passage.

title: Embeddings and Vector Search
text: Embedding models convert text into numeric vectors that preserve semantic similarity. Retrieval systems compare a query vector with document vectors using cosine similarity or dot product. TF-IDF is a sparse lexical baseline, while neural embeddings improve semantic matching.

title: Reranking Retrieved Context
text: A reranker takes the initial retrieved candidates and scores them with a more precise model. Reranking can improve precision at small K by moving the most relevant passages to the top of the context window. It is often used after fast approximate retrieval.

title: RAG Evaluation Metrics
text: RAG evaluation measures both retrieval quality and answer quality. Retrieval can be scored with Recall@K, Precision@K, Hit Rate, MRR, and NDCG. Answer quality can be measured with keyword coverage, citation support, faithfulness checks, and human review.

title: RAG Latency and Cost
text: Production RAG systems must track latency and cost. Index lookup, reranking, prompt construction, and generation each add latency. Caching, smaller context windows, batching, and cheaper embedding models can reduce cost while preserving answer quality.

title: RAG Guardrails
text: RAG systems need guardrails for unsupported questions and low-confidence retrieval. A system can decline to answer when retrieval scores are weak, when citations are missing, or when the generated answer includes claims not supported by retrieved context.

title: RAG Experiment Tracking
text: Experiment tracking helps compare chunk sizes, retrieval models, rerankers, prompts, and top-k values. Useful experiment logs include dataset version, retrieval metrics, answer metrics, latency, and qualitative failure cases.
